title: Woodstock: The Festival for Stardust, Golden Hippies
summary: Josh and Chuck explore the 1969 Woodstock Music and Art Fair: why it drew 400,000 to 500,000 people to Bethel, New York; how promoters Artie Cornfeld, Michael Lang, John Roberts and Joel Rosenman pushed it through with local permits and a five-week build; how Max Yasgur's farm hosted it; the decision to make it free; the Hog Farm and Wavy Gravy's peacekeeping; Chip Monck's announcements about brown acid; the performers (Richie Havens opening, Santana, Grateful Dead, CCR, The Who, Jimi Hendrix's Monday morning set); the medical and volunteer effort; the cleanup; the deaths; the finances and the 1970 documentary. The episode also includes a listener mail from Tom and his seven-year-old son John.
topics: Jimi Hendrix Star Spangled Banner Woodstock

segments.title: Opening banter on Woodstock and Joni Mitchell's song
segments.summary: Hosts open with banter about the Woodstock song (written by Joni Mitchell), a cover by Matthews' Southern Comfort, and their general impressions of the 1969 festival and its size.

segments.title: Why Woodstock was special and its location
segments.summary: The hosts explain the festival's location within driving distance of major cities, why it was named Woodstock despite being held in Bethel, and the artistic town's ties to Bob Dylan and The Band.

segments.title: Origins of the music festival and its promoters
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the history of jazz and pop festivals, Monterey Pop, the Altamont decline and the revival by Lollapalooza, and then the founders Cornfeld, Lang, Roberts and Rosenman, whose original plan was a benefit concert for a studio.

segments.title: Finding a site and Max Yasgur
segments.summary: After rejected sites including Woodstock, Saugerties and Wallkill, dairy farmer Max Yasgur offered his Bethel farm. The promoters obtained permits by making promises to local officials they did not intend to keep.

segments.title: Five-week build, budget and lineup
segments.summary: The promoters had five weeks to build the stage and infrastructure, ticket pricing was discussed, and the hosts cover which major acts played or didn't, and how Woodstock boosted lesser-known performers.

segments.title: Santana and Neil Sean connection tangent
segments.summary: The hosts discuss Santana's Woodstock appearance arranged through Bill Graham, and a tangent about Journey founder Neil Schon having been in Santana as a teenager.

segments.title: Decision to make Woodstock free and the fencing problem
segments.summary: With fifty thousand people camped at the site by midweek and the stage unfinished, the promoters announced the festival would be free. The hosts discuss how this prevented gate-crashing and shaped the festival's vibe.

segments.title: Traffic, food shortages and community help
segments.summary: Cars were abandoned along roads and attendees walked to the site. Food and water ran out and nearby towns, the National Guard, the Army and Max Yasgur helped supply it, and locals made sandwiches.

segments.title: Hog Farm, Chip Monck and brown acid warnings
segments.summary: The Hog Farm commune, led by Wavy Gravy, provided peaceful security and services. Chip Monck served as MC and made the famous brown acid warning. Medical volunteers came in, and the hosts discuss the rain, bad trips and the use of Valium.

segments.title: Performances: Richie Havens, Santana, Grateful Dead, CCR, Neil Young
segments.summary: The hosts discuss notable performances, including Richie Havens opening, Santana playing on mescaline or acid, the Grateful Dead's loose set, CCR's Fogerty, and Crosby, Stills, Nash and Young's omission from the film. A short anecdote about a Grateful Dead refund follows.

segments.title: The Who, Shaha Na Na, Jimi Hendrix and the cleanup
segments.summary: The Who's surly performance and monitor problems and Abbie Hoffman's stage interruption. Shana Na Na's fifties set, Van Halen singing Happy Trails, Jimi Hendrix's Monday morning Star Spangled Banner, volunteers who cleaned the site, and the finances and documentary.

segments.title: Deaths, legacy, Max Yasgur's speech and the Woodstock baby legend
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the two deaths at the festival, comparison with Buffalo's weekend death count, the Woodstock baby legend, Max Yasgur's speech to the crowd, and later Woodstock revivals.

segments.title: Listener mail from Tom and son John
segments.summary: A listener writes that his seven-year-old son John believes the hosts are married because they get along well. The hosts respond.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts sign off and thank listeners, with the show credit and listener-mail address.
